title: SRE weekly heuristic notebook — Sept 13 2030
content:
Purpose
Quick field notebook for the week: capture operational hypotheses, SLO signal anomalies, short post-incident notes, and the next set of small experiments we want on the token-service and autoscale heuristics. Not a formal postmortem — that will land under INC-8274 — but a working log for the on-call and the latency triage squad.

Summary (top-line)
- Incident: token-service soft-degradation on 2030-09-11 03:20 UTC causing 95th p99 token latency jump from 120ms -> 420ms for ~18 minutes. No client-visible errors, just increased tail latency.
- Root-candidate: contention in shared KV-store when prefix-cache invalidation spike coincided with a config rollout. Secondary contributor: batching heuristic misprediction (small batches created many small writes).
- Impact: some hosted-api customers saw short-lived latency spikes; Dedicated clusters with pinned capacity unaffected. No SLO burn beyond alert thresholds for error rate but we crossed latency SLO for a ~20-min window.

Incidents log (brief)
- 2030-09-11 03:20 UTC — p99 starts climbing. Pager page triggered at 03:25 when p99 >= 350ms for 5m. Bridge created. On-call: Aisha. (INC-8274)
  - 03:27: Ops toggled token-cache-read-only mode (hotfix) — partial mitigation.
  - 03:33: Noticed config rollout to kernel-optimizer group on the same zero-downtime path; rollback initiated at 03:36.
  - 03:40: p99 trending down slowly; full recovery by 03:52. Post-incident telemetry attached to JIRA.

Observations + Signals
- Metric spikes: kv-store write-latency, token-service GC pause count, and small-batch-write rate spiked simultaneously. Suggests a multi-component interaction.
- Trace sampling: 75% of high-latency traces show >4 cross-service RPC hops with queued waits on kv-store client.
- Canary signals: internal canary showed 40% p50 increase before external customers hit thresholds — we need earlier alerting on canary tail.

Immediate action items (owner, due)
- Add an early-warning rule for kv-store write-latency 95th crossing 90ms for 3m to paged channel: owner Jon Kim, due 2030-09-16.
- Patch batching heuristic to avoid falling back to tiny batches under low backlog when autoscale flush is scheduled: owner Priya Rao, PR under ENG-1938, due 2030-09-20.
- Improve canary tail monitoring (note: current canary uses p50 and p95; we want p99-p999 monitoring for token-service): owner Evan Brooks, due 2030-09-18.
- Add a quick-runbook step to pause non-urgent config rollouts if kv-store 95th > 120ms: owner Marcos Alvarez (me), due 2030-09-17.

SLO snapshot (week-to-date)
- Token-service latency SLO (p95 <= 200ms): currently 99.81% over rolling 7d, but the 18-min window on 09-11 caused a localized burn. We didn't cross the 99% alert window yet but it's close for the daily bucket.
- Hosted API availability SLO: 99.96% 7d; unaffected.
- Dedicated cluster tail-latency SLO measured separately and remains healthy.

Handoff notes for next on-call (what to scan first)
- Quick checklist (first 10 minutes):
  1) Open dashboards: token-service-overview, kv-store-latency, autoscale-flush-events.
  2) Confirm canary p99 trend; if canary p99 rises >50% from baseline, escalate to core-sre.
  3) Check open config-rollout queue in config-service and any pending kernel optimizer rollouts.
  4) Verify batching-heuristic metrics: small_batch_rate and flush-trigger-count.

Heuristic experiments (short log)
- Experiment A: staggered config-apply windows. Hypothesis: applying small config changes in staggered windows reduces peak concurrent invalidations that stress kv-store. Quick test: pick 5 internal non-customer-facing rollouts and stagger them over 15m windows. Owner: Jon. Status: queued.
- Experiment B: opportunistic batch coalescing. When backlog low but next flush scheduled soon, hold micro-requests for up to 30ms to allow coalescing into larger writes — reduces write QPS. Risk: slight added p50 latency. Owner: Priya. Simulated in dev; promising.
- Experiment C: ephemeral client-side kv cache with read-through fuzzing. Small TTL (~2s) to smooth bursts of reads during invalidation storms. Owner: Evan. WIP.

Playbook gaps we spotted
- No explicit run for combined-rollout + kv-store-stress scenario. Current runbooks treat config rollout and kv store separately. Add a composed runbook with decision tree: rollback vs pause rollout vs apply backoff. Owner: Marcos. Target: 2030-09-21.
- Alert fatigue: pagers currently trigger on p95 crosses for several services; need to route the kv-store early-warning to non-pager after-hours channel first, escalate if persists. This reduces noisy wakeups and focuses on sustained issues. Owner: SRE leadership (working with ops).

Meeting notes (weekly on-call sync — 2030-09-13 16:00 UTC)
Attendees: Marcos (chair), Aisha (on-call), Jon, Priya, Evan, Caroline (service-owner), Dana (product)
Key decisions:
- Prioritize batching heuristic patch (ENG-1938) for next deploy; block other non-critical kernel-optimizer rollouts until patch stabilizes.
- Create a short-term canary p99 monitor and wire it to the slack-alerts/sre-watch channel (non-pager by default). Evan to own.
- Pilot staggered-rollouts on a single infra zone next week; if stable, expand. Jon to schedule.
Open questions:
- Is there a capacity planning signal we can add to prevent config rollouts during known high-traffic windows for specific customers? (Dana)
- Are there any long-lived KV clients we can rework to use TTL-based ephemeral caches? Caroline to list top three candidates.

Notes to self (freeform)
- Think about adding a simple probe that mimics a small chain of RPCs to reproduce the cross-service queued waits in staging. Might be able to catch the interaction earlier in CI if we simulate simultaneous invalidations + small-batch writes.
- Consider a micro-metric that tracks "concurrent-prefix-invalidations" — count of prefix invalidations within sliding 1m window. Could be the earliest signal.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Full traces (sampled high-latency): https://observability.redwood/trace/INC-8274-sample
- Incident ticket: JIRA INC-8274
- Batching heuristic patch: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1427
- Config rollout tracker: confluence://deploys/rollout-queue-2030-09

Action log (short)
- 2030-09-13: Jon created early-warning alert draft (PR in alerts repo) — awaiting review.
- 2030-09-13: Priya opened ENG-1938 and deployed candidate to staging.
- 2030-09-14: Marcos drafted composed-runbook page (needs diagrams).
If you're reading this as the next on-call: don't be shy about calling for a pause on rollouts if kv-store tail starts climbing. Small conservative action early avoids long noisy burn windows.

End of notebook entry.
